name: Trans fatty acids
aliases: trans fats, trans fatty acids, partially hydrogenated oil, partially hydrogenated vegetable oil, iTFAs, grasas trans
what_is: Trans fats are a type of unsaturated fat. Industrial ones are formed mainly by partially hydrogenating oils to make them more solid, stable and longer-lasting, which is why they can be found in pastries, biscuits, fried foods, margarines and other processed products. On a label they may appear as trans fats or, more often, as partially hydrogenated oil or fat. Small amounts also occur naturally in the meat and dairy of ruminant animals.
why_botia: WHO states that trans fats have no known health benefit and that they increase the risk of coronary heart disease, heart attack and death. It recommends they provide less than 1% of daily energy, and that industrial trans fats be eliminated from foods. In a cohort of 18,555 women, for every 2% of daily energy in which trans fats replaced carbohydrates, the risk of ovulatory infertility was 73% higher, and more than double when they replaced monounsaturated fats.
can_1: Detect partially hydrogenated oils or an explicit trans-fat declaration when they appear on the label.
can_2: Explain what WHO says about trans fats and what the cohort in women found, and show the Woman information layer.
cannot_1: Determine the exact amount of trans fat from an ingredient list when the quantity is not declared.
cannot_2: Prove that trans-fat intake caused infertility in a particular person.

sources.label: Cohort: trans fat intake and ovulatory infertility (2019)

title: Trans fatty acids
description: Trans fats are formed mainly by partially hydrogenating oils, and appear on labels as trans fats or partially hydrogenated oil. WHO says they have no known health benefit and recommends eliminating the industrial ones. In a cohort of 18,555 women, higher intake was associated with more ovulatory infertility.
